lines.japanese: 朝のラッシュアワー。
lines.english: Morning rush hour.

lines.japanese: 地上を走る地下鉄は、シーズン終盤のスポーツ選手みたいに疲れの溜まった乗客を、今日もたっぷり詰めこんでいた。
lines.english: The aboveground subway was packed again today with passengers carrying fatigue like athletes late in the season.

lines.japanese: しかし電車通学三年目にもなれば、乗車率２００％超えの混雑にも不感症でいられる。
lines.english: But in my third year of commuting by train, even a crowd at over two hundred percent capacity could leave me numb.
“Phew...”

lines.japanese: ベテランの手際で首尾よくドア前のスペースを確保した僕は、ひやりと冷たい窓ガラスに額を──
lines.english: With a veteran's skill, I secured a place by the doors and lowered my forehead toward the chilly window glass—

lines.japanese: 「──うわっ」
lines.english: “—Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 「きゃっ」
lines.english: “Eek!”

lines.japanese: 失態だ。重心の安定をおろそかにしてしまったその瞬間、カーブに差しかかった車体が激しく揺れた。
lines.english: A blunder. At the very moment I neglected to steady my center of gravity, the train entered a curve and lurched violently.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん」
lines.english: “Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえっ……」
lines.english: “O-Oh, no...”

lines.japanese: 小さな悲鳴をあげたすぐ横の下級生に詫びる。混雑で体が密着していたから、僕が傾いたことで彼女にも衝撃を与えてしまったんだ。
lines.english: I apologized to the younger girl beside me who had given the little cry. The crush had our bodies pressed together, so when I tipped sideways, the impact carried into her too.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 知ってる子の気がして、よく確認しようとしたら、頭ごと下を向かれてしまった。
lines.english: I thought I recognized her and tried to look more closely, but she ducked her whole head.

lines.japanese: だけどその慌てように覚えがあって、思いだすことができた。よくこの車両に乗っている、可愛らしい二年生。ちょっと前に、足を踏んづけられたりしたこともある。
lines.english: Yet her panic was familiar enough to bring the memory back. She was the cute second-year who often rode in this car. Not long ago, she had even stepped on my foot.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、どうも」
lines.english: “Oh. Hello.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は俯いたまま無言で会釈した。
lines.english: She kept her head lowered and answered with a silent bow.

lines.japanese: ほとんどあしらうような反応だ。僕を覚えていないのかもしれない。こっちだって今の今まで気付いていなかったのだから、ひとのことはそう言えないけれど。
lines.english: It was almost a dismissive response. Perhaps she didn't remember me. I could hardly criticize her when I myself had failed to notice her until this very moment.

lines.japanese: 言えないのだけれど、ちょっと、残念だな。
lines.english: I couldn't criticize her, but it was still a little disappointing.

lines.japanese: 手持ち無沙汰な通学時間を、下級生との歓談で華やかにいろどることもなく。
lines.english: There would be no pleasant chat with a younger student to brighten an otherwise idle commute.

lines.japanese: しかし車窓から望む１２月の白い空は、さほど高くも感じられなかった。
lines.english: Even so, the white December sky beyond the window didn't seem particularly high above me.

lines.japanese: 何故って世界は平和だから。
lines.english: Because the world was at peace.

lines.japanese: そう。空も学校も意外と平和だったんだ。
lines.english: Yes. The sky and the school were surprisingly peaceful.

lines.japanese: 少なくとも僕が思いこんでいたよりはずっと。
lines.english: Far more so than I had once believed.

lines.japanese: ちょうど校門をくぐった足元に、ころころとソフトボールが転がってきた。
lines.english: Just as I passed through the school gate, a softball came rolling to my feet.

lines.japanese: 追いかけてくる制服の男子を認めて、僕は先にボールを拾いあげる。
lines.english: I saw the uniformed boy chasing it and picked up the ball first.

lines.japanese: 「おう、悪りぃ羽田！」
lines.english: “Hey, sorry, Haneda!”

lines.japanese: 軽く走りながら片手をあげたのは、同じクラスの鴻野君だった。元運動部の仲間と、制服のままちょっとした朝の運動をしてるみたい。
lines.english: Kono, one of my classmates, raised a hand as he jogged over. It looked like he was getting a little morning exercise in uniform with friends from his old sports club.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう。いくよっ」
lines.english: “Good morning. Here you go.”

lines.japanese: 僕は挨拶しながら下手投げでボールを放った。彼は両手で受けとめると──
lines.english: I greeted him and tossed the ball underhand. He caught it in both hands, then—

lines.japanese: 「カノッサの屈辱！」
lines.english: “The Walk to Canossa!”

lines.japanese: ──とつぜん年号問題を挑んできた。うちのクラスの世界史を選択している男子のあいだでは、この時期、わりと日常的なやり取りだ。
lines.english: —suddenly challenged me for its date. Among the boys in our class who had chosen world history, exchanges like this were fairly routine at this time of year.

lines.japanese: 異例な難儀、かのヘンリー氏。さほど勉強していない僕でも、このぐらいの基本は覚えてる。
lines.english: Ten seventy-seven: poor Henry’s frozen road to heaven. Even without much studying, I knew a basic one like that.

lines.japanese: 「くっそ、正解！」
lines.english: “Damn it, right!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ベルリン会議は？」
lines.english: “Then what about the Congress of Berlin?”

lines.japanese: 「近代かよ……俺ニガテなんだよ、近代……」
lines.english: “Modern history...? I suck at modern history...”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　鴻野君、近世も中世も古代も苦手って言ってなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Huh? Didn't you say you were bad at early modern, medieval, and ancient history too?”

lines.japanese: 「うっせえ。あー、ベルリン会議だろ、１８……６８年？」
lines.english: “Shut up. Uh, the Congress of Berlin. Eighteen... sixty-eight?”
“Sorry. Seventy-eight.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわ、十年早かったかー！」
lines.english: “Aw, man! Ten years too early!”

lines.japanese: 「おれに勝つのも十年早いってことかなあ」
lines.english: “Maybe you're ten years too early to beat me.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえ、上手くねえよ。チクショ覚えてろ、次はぜってー勝つかんな」
lines.english: “Shut up. That wasn't clever. Damn it, just you wait. I'm definitely winning next time.”

lines.japanese: んじゃ、と言って鴻野君は仲間のもとへ走っていった。
lines.english: “Later,” Kono said, and ran back to his friends.

lines.japanese: ほら、こんな風に。空も学校も世界も、かつて僕が思いこんでいたよりは平和なものだったんだ。
lines.english: See? Just like that. The sky, the school, and the world were all more peaceful than I had once believed.

lines.japanese: 千歳君や成田君が内側の曇りを晴らしてくれた。
lines.english: Chitose and Narita had cleared the clouds within me.

lines.japanese: 森里君が世界の器用な歩き方を教えてくれた。
lines.english: Morisato had taught me how to navigate the world with ease.

lines.japanese: 針生さんは世界の広さを教えてくれた。
lines.english: Hariu had taught me how vast the world was.

lines.japanese: 山科さんは世界の痛みを教えてくれた。
lines.english: Yamashina had taught me the pain in the world.

lines.japanese: 高内さんは世界の厳しさを教えてくれた。
lines.english: Takauchi had taught me the harshness of the world.

lines.japanese: そして渡来さんが、世界は金色に輝いていることを教えてくれた。
lines.english: And Watarai had taught me that the world shone gold.

lines.japanese: いろんなひとが、僕に世界の何たるかを教えてくれたんだ。
lines.english: So many people had taught me what the world was.

lines.japanese: 「委員長おはよー」
lines.english: “Morning, Class Rep.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、おはよう」
lines.english: “Oh, good morning.”

lines.japanese: 昇降口を抜けたところで会ったのは、同じクラスの川野さんだった。
lines.english: The person I met after passing through the entrance was Kawano, another classmate.

lines.japanese: 「ひとり？　渡来さんは？」
lines.english: “By yourself? Where's Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、いつも一緒なわけじゃないよ。おれ、おまけじゃないもん」
lines.english: “We aren't always together. I'm not an accessory.”

lines.japanese: 「とか言って、委員長さびしそー。泣いてんじゃないのー？」
lines.english: “You say that, but you look looonesome. Are you gonna cry?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いま川野さんにいじめられて泣きそう」
lines.english: “Yes. You’re picking on me right now, Kawano. I might cry.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、委員長いじめんの楽しー」
lines.english: “Ahaha. It’s fun picking on you, Class Rep.”

lines.japanese: じゃあね、と言って川野さんはよその組の友達を追いかけて行った。
lines.english: “See you,” Kawano said, and hurried after a friend from another class.

lines.japanese: 「羽田ぁ～」
lines.english: “Hanedaaa.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、藤野君。おはよう」
lines.english: “Oh, Fujino. Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 教室の前で会ったのは、同じクラスの藤野君だった。
lines.english: The person I met in front of the classroom was Fujino, another classmate.

lines.japanese: 「なァー、氷のダンジョンのボス倒せねンだよ。鬼じゃんアレ」
lines.english: “Hey, I can't beat the boss in the ice dungeon. That thing's brutal.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あそこはファイア系の魔法がないとキツイよね。とりあえず後回しにして、サブクエストでフレイムソード取ってからの方がいいかも」
lines.english: “Oh, that part's tough without fire magic. You might want to leave it for now and get the Flame Sword from the side quest first.”

lines.japanese: 「マジ？　サブクエでそんな強ええ武器出ンだ？　ヘェ～、俺めんどくさくてネットの攻略法とか見ねーからなあ」
lines.english: “Seriously? You get a weapon that strong from a side quest? Huh. I can't be bothered looking up walkthroughs online.”

lines.japanese: 「おれもそんなには見ないけどね。あんまり詳しくもないし、うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “I don't look at them that much either. I'm not especially knowledgeable. I'm pretty average, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「普通じゃねーだろ、オメー引くほど詳しいだろ」
lines.english: “Average, my ass. You know so much it's disturbing.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、ばれてたかあ」
lines.english: “Ahaha. You caught me.”

lines.japanese: 僕は藤野君に笑ってみせながら教室へ入った。
lines.english: I smiled at Fujino and entered the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「うーっす、羽田」
lines.english: “Yo, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、おはよう」
lines.english: “Oh, good morning.”

lines.japanese: 席へ着いた僕に声をかけてくれたのは、女子の学級委員・高内さんだった。
lines.english: The girl who greeted me when I reached my seat was Takauchi, the other class representative.

lines.japanese: 卒業文集を完成させたぐらいのころから、彼女が僕を訪れる機会は増えたような気がする。
lines.english: Ever since around the time we finished the graduation anthology, I felt as though she had begun coming to see me more often.

lines.japanese: もし級友として認めてもらえたのだとしたら、それはとても嬉しいことだ。
lines.english: If that meant she had accepted me as a classmate, it made me very happy.

lines.japanese: 「あんさー、担任に雑用押しつけられちゃったんだけどー。私、部活の用とかもあってー。ちょっと手ぇいっぱいなんだよねー」
lines.english: “So, the homeroom teacher dumped some busywork on me, but I've got club stuff too. My hands are kinda full.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん。いいよ、おれがやっておく」
lines.english: “Oh, sure. That's fine. I'll take care of it.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。いいの？」
lines.english: “Huh. You don't mind?”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ？　おれだって学級委員なんだし」
lines.english: “Why would I? I'm a class representative too.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうなんだけど……いいの、そんなんで」
lines.english: “Yeah, I know... But are you sure you're okay with that?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、用事があるなら仕方ないよ、困ったときはお互い様だし」
lines.english: “If you have something else to do, it can't be helped. We should help each other when we're in trouble.”

lines.japanese: 「つったって、用とかそんな、私の嘘かもしんねーじゃん。おまえ騙されて使われてるだけかもしんねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Yeah, but that whole thing about having somewhere to be could be a lie. Maybe I'm just tricking you and using you.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そうなの？」
lines.english: “What? Are you?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、違げーけど。用あんのはガチだけど」
lines.english: “No, I'm not. I really do have stuff to do.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょ？　高内さんはちょっと怖いけど、意味もなく嫌なことをするようなひとではないと思う」
lines.english: “See? You can be a little scary, Takauchi, but I don’t think you’d be nasty for no reason.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ……バカジャネーノおまえ、おめでたいにも程があんだろ」
lines.english: “Y-You stupid or what? There's a limit to how trusting you can be.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それはよく言われちゃうんだ。でも、無闇にひとを疑うぐらいだったら、おれは馬鹿のままでいたいって思う」
lines.english: “Yes, people tell me that a lot. But if the alternative is suspecting people for no reason, I'd rather remain a fool.”

lines.japanese: 「あっそ。じゃ悪いけど今回は頼むわ。ありがとな」
lines.english: “Whatever. Sorry, but I'm leaving it to you this time. Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは去った。
lines.english: Takauchi left.

lines.japanese: だけどすぐ戻ってきた。
lines.english: But she came right back.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ……あんた、さっき私のこと怖いッつった？」
lines.english: “Hey... Did you just say I was scary?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジ？　怖い？」
lines.english: “Seriously? I'm scary?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ときどき」
lines.english: “Sometimes.”

lines.japanese: 「つーと、どーゆーとこが」
lines.english: “Like, what part of me?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、全体的に」
lines.english: “Hmm. All of you.”

lines.japanese: 「とくに顔」
lines.english: “Especially your face.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、顔な……顔はまあ、そりゃなァ。美人が怒ると怖いってゆーし？」
lines.english: “O-Oh, my face... Well, sure. They say beautiful women are scary when they're angry, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あはははは美人って」
lines.english: “Ahahahaha. Beautiful.”

lines.japanese: 「テメ笑うとこじゃねーんだよ。あ？　シメられてえのか、あ？　あ？」
lines.english: “That ain't the part you laugh at. Huh? You want me to mess you up? Do you?”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほら怖い……顔が怖いよ高内さん……」
lines.english: “S-See? Scary... Your face is scary, Takauchi...”

lines.japanese: 左右非対称の形相でじりじり詰めよってくるものだから、大きく張りだした胸が当たらないよう、僕は身を引かなければならなかった。
lines.english: She crept toward me with her face twisted asymmetrically, forcing me to lean back so that her generously protruding chest wouldn't touch me.

lines.japanese: 「んー、どしたこらー」
lines.english: “Hmm? What’s all this, then?”

lines.japanese: 古文の金子先生の口真似をしながら渡来さんがやってきた。
lines.english: Watarai arrived while impersonating Kaneko, our classical Japanese teacher.

lines.japanese: 「ねー、なんだっけ、こないだ羽田君が言ってたアニメ。昨日だったんだよね、また見逃しちゃった」
lines.english: “Hey, what was that anime you mentioned the other day, Haneda? It was on yesterday, right? I missed it again.”

lines.japanese: 唐突に高内さんの入れない話を始めたのは、きっと僕を救いだすためなんだろう。
lines.english: She had probably brought up a subject that excluded Takauchi so abruptly in order to rescue me.

lines.japanese: 「ちっ」
lines.english: “Tch.”

lines.japanese: その思惑を察してか、高内さんは健全な間合いに戻っていった。ありがとう渡来さん。
lines.english: Perhaps recognizing her intention, Takauchi retreated to a healthy distance. Thank you, Watarai.

lines.japanese: けれど、それはそれとして、僕は彼女と趣味を共有できる機会に胸が躍った。
lines.english: That aside, my heart leaped at the chance to share one of my interests with her.

lines.japanese: なぜなら、僕が自信を持って勧めるアニメやゲームに、これまで渡来さんが興味を示したことはほとんどなかったからだ。
lines.english: After all, Watarai had almost never shown any interest in the anime and games I recommended with confidence.

lines.japanese: 「昨日っていうと『軟式文芸部！』でしょ、あれはいいよ、ぜったい観るべき」
lines.english: “If you mean yesterday, that was Soft Lit Club! It's great. You absolutely have to watch it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あーそう。まあ、立たなくてもいいけど」
lines.english: “O-Oh, okay. You don't have to stand up, though.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、でも、本当に観た方がいいと思うよ。話はよくある日常のユル萌え系なんだけど、空気がいいっていうか、キャラ立てとか見せ方がとにかく神なんだ」
lines.english: “Right, but I really think you should watch it. It’s the usual laid-back slice-of-life story about cute girls, but the atmosphere is great. And the characters and presentation are just godlike.”

lines.japanese: 「神？　宗教の話？」
lines.english: “Godlike? Is it about religion?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ、原作は鬱串ヶ原メギドさんの部活系４コマだよ。やる気のない女子部員が、部室でごろごろしたり家でごろごろしたり、寝たり食べたりごろごろしたりするんだ」
lines.english: “No. It’s based on Megiddo Utsukushigahara’s four-panel manga about a school club. The girls have no motivation. They laze around the clubroom, laze around at home, sleep, eat, and laze around some more.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、高内の話か」
lines.english: “Oh. It's about Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。私、萌え系だったのかよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? I’m one of the cute girls?”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！　やめなよ渡来さん、冗談でも鬱串ヶ原先生に失礼だよ」
lines.english: “What?! Stop that, Watarai. Even as a joke, that's insulting to Utsukushigahara.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　そらテメ、どーゆー意味だコラ、あ？　あ？」
lines.english: “Huh? And what's that supposed to mean, asshole? Huh? Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だから、怖いよ高内さん……ほら、顔が恐いってば……」
lines.english: “T-That's what I mean. You're scary, Takauchi... Look, your face is scary...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、分かった分かった。そんなに言うなら来週は観るよ。ま、忘れてなければね」
lines.english: “Fine, fine. If you insist that much, I'll watch it next week. If I remember.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、おれが放映５分前になったら電話してあげる」
lines.english: “Don't worry. I'll call you five minutes before it airs.”

lines.japanese: 「高内ー、夜中の２時にアニメ点けろって電話してくる彼氏、どう思う？」
lines.english: “Takauchi, what would you think of a boyfriend who calls at two in the morning to tell you to turn on an anime?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、渡来ン家ビデオとかねーの？」
lines.english: “Wait, don't you have a VCR or something at your place?”

lines.japanese: 「んや、最新のＤＶＤレコーダー持ってる」
lines.english: “No, I've got the latest DVD recorder.”

lines.japanese: 「あんじゃん」
lines.english: “Then there you go.”

lines.japanese: 「でもテレビに接続してないんだよね」
lines.english: “But it isn't connected to the TV.”

lines.japanese: 「持ってるだけかよ」
lines.english: “So you just own the thing?”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ない。女子は機械に弱いって、昔から相場が決まってるんだ」
lines.english: “Can’t help it. Everybody knows girls are bad with machines.”

lines.japanese: 「機械ってほどのモンかよ、家電だろ。そんぐれーマニュアル見りゃ誰だって出来るっての」
lines.english: “That barely counts as a machine. It's an appliance. Anybody can hook that much up if they read the manual.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ。だからこないだ行ったとき、おれが繋いであげるって言ったのに」
lines.english: “Exactly. That's why I offered to connect it the last time I was there.”

lines.japanese: 「あんときは、だって、羽田君スポーツニュース観てたじゃん」
lines.english: “But you were watching sports news that time, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あれは渡来さんのお風呂が長かったから、適当に点けてただけだよ。先に寝ちゃわないように」
lines.english: “That was only because you were taking so long in the bath. I turned on whatever was there to keep myself from falling asleep.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、寝てても良かったのに」
lines.english: “I wouldn't have minded if you'd been asleep.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、でも、そのあとに……その、僕なりに予定っていうか、ちょっと、希望もあったし……」
lines.english: “I know, but afterward... Well, I had plans of my own, or perhaps I should say... hopes...”

lines.japanese: 「あー、私そーいや用あるんだったー」
lines.english: “Oh, that's right. I just remembered I had somewhere to be.”

lines.japanese: 気付いたら高内さんは消えていた。
lines.english: By the time I noticed, Takauchi had vanished.

lines.japanese: 僕と渡来さんもなんとなく気まずくなってしまい、なんとなく解散した。
lines.english: Watarai and I had somehow ended up feeling awkward too, and somehow drifted apart.
